courses.title: University Writing
courses.course_description: A study of the use of writing, reading, and discussion as a means of discovering, questioning, and analyzing ideas, with an emphasis on audience, context and the use of revision. This course satisfies the Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement. It does not satisfy a general education requirement in the Humanities and Social or Behavioral Sciences.

courses.title: Univ Writ Multilingual Studnt
courses.course_description: This course is designed to help international students develop skills in writing, reading and discussion as a means of discovering, questioning and analyzing ideas. Students will engage in reading a variety of texts on a theme, extrapolating key ideas, and developing their own claims through discussion, research writing, and presentation. Additionally, this course will provide support to address common writing issues for multilingual speakers of English as well as build intercultural competence in communication. Placement in this course is based on English proficiency and/or placement exam results. Equivalent to COM 101. This course satisfies IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement. It does not satisfy a general education requirement in the humanities and social or behavioral sciences.

courses.title: Chicago Voices
courses.course_description: This English communication course will give international students the opportunity to expand their knowledge of Chicago’s history and culture while developing their voice through advanced conversation, presentation, and discussion skills. Through a storytelling and experiential lens, students will focus on articulating and responding to in-depth questions, applying advanced presentation skills, and using cultural and communicative skills to collaborate in dynamic city-focused discussions. Placement in this course is based on English proficiency and/or placement exam results.

courses.title: Telling Your Story
courses.course_description: This course focuses on the most important topic of all: YOU! You have a unique story to tell – whether in an interview, a discussion, or a professional presentation – and this course will give students the opportunity to develop advanced language skills around each student’s field of study and interests. Through engaging with audio and video materials, active reading, and intensive speaking practice, students will work to develop personalized responses to a variety of behavioral interview questions, research and contribute information from their individual fields into a group discussion, as well as write and present on a technical topic to a general audience of students. Placement in this course is based on English proficiency and/or placement exam results.

courses.title: Rhetoric, Argumnt & Persuasion
courses.course_description: Arguments are a tool we use to build our social realities and the worlds we want to see. In this course, we move beyond “winning debates” to instead ask: How does culture and context convince us what is true, and how do we critically assess those assumptions? Using an interdisciplinary blend of theories and methods from the humanities and social sciences, we will analyze argumentation as a contest over power. We will explore how “common sense” is constructed through discursive repetition and ritual, as well as how media technologies have historically (and in the present) facilitated those constructions. Students will learn to navigate the politics of representation, scrutinize the “mythologies” of Big Tech, and construct arguments that are not only logical, but socially and ethically responsive to the conditions of the world.

courses.title: Media History and Theory
courses.course_description: This course will examine how communication technologies have evolved from the printing press to the digital age. Students will explore the impact of these technologies on society, culture, and political movements critically, with special emphasis placed on the importance of social media and digital culture to contemporary society.

courses.title: Information Literacy
courses.course_description: Information Literacy and Sense-Making instills students with the skills essential to be information-savvy professionals. Key concepts include the location and vetting of primary, secondary, and tertiary sources; fact checking and provenance; and the integration of disparate information sources into cohesive, fact-based forms and tools such as reports, memos, and research papers.

courses.title: Ethics of Tech & Communication
courses.course_description: In this course, we will investigate philosophical questions about the nature of technology and communication, as well as ethical questions related to a broad range of specific communication-related technologies. Topics include algorithmic bias and fairness, privacy and surveillance, consent and manipulation, and the environmental impacts of digital technologies. Students will engage with case studies that require applying ethical principles to complex situations.

courses.course_description: An introduction to the art of public speaking with assignments designed to promote competency in the delivery of speeches, organization of ideas, methods of argumentation, application of evidence and use of visual aids.

courses.title: The Human Voice
courses.course_description: Analysis of human and synthetic speech intended for technology mediated environments and devices. Focus on talker characteristics that affect speech intelligibility and social factors that affect talker characteristics. Attention to design characteristics of technology-mediated speech and how humans react to it.

courses.title: Discourse Analysis
courses.course_description: The analysis of language "flow" beyond sentence boundaries. Working with both spoken and written discourse, students will consider culture and gender-related patterns, and will apply findings from discourse analysis to communication problems in politics, education, healthcare, and the law.

courses.title: A.I.-Assisted Workflows
courses.course_description: AI-Assisted Workflows prepares students to work effectively with AI tools across communication tasks including content generation, research, editing, and analysis. Topics include prompt engineering, critical evaluation of AI outputs, workflow integration, and maintaining appropriate human oversight. Explicitly addresses limitations, risks, and ethical dimensions of AI tools. Emphasis on AI as a tool to be directed rather than a replacement for human judgment.

courses.title: Technical Communication
courses.course_description: Principles and practice in the communication of technical materials. Students work on the design, writing, and revising of reports, articles, manuals, procedures, proposals, including the use of graphics. Works by modern writers are analyzed.

Emphasis on usability, cohesion, and style in each assignment.

Special attention is paid to analyzing and evaluating academic journals and conferences; submitting items to journals and conferences; navigating the research, writing, and publication process; revising work and providing feedback to others; and mastering the conventions of academic writing.
